title: Receipt Desk Worksheet: The Revised Pledge on a Reduced Warehouse Receipt
content:
The pledge is reduced by the bushels the largest signed load-out request standing received on the agreement names, and where that would take the pledge below nothing the pledge is taken to nothing and the receipt is surrendered. This worksheet covers Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements.

## The revised figure

The revised pledge is the bushels left on the receipt plus every margin the elevator keeps standing, the sum taken to no less than nothing and rounded to two decimal places.

The margins and the holdbacks are added to the bushels left on the receipt rather than one acting on another's result, and the rounding up is done once, on the total.

## Reading the request

The bushels taken off the pledge are those named by the largest of the member's signed load-out requests standing received on that agreement. Where the agreement carries several such requests, the largest is the one read; where the quantity it names is greater than what stands pledged, the pledge is taken to nothing and the receipt is surrendered rather than reduced.

## Worked figure, on hypothetical quantities

An agreement carries 18000 bushels standing pledged under a receipt. Two signed load-out requests stand received on it, one naming 4000 bushels and one naming 6500.

1. The largest request names 6500 bushels.
2. Eighteen thousand less six thousand five hundred leaves 11500 bushels on the receipt, which is above nothing, so the receipt is reduced rather than surrendered.
3. With no margin standing, the revised pledge is 11500, rounded to two decimal places 11500.00.

## A second worked figure

The same agreement carries 5200 bushels standing pledged, and the largest signed load-out request standing received names 7000 bushels. Five thousand two hundred less seven thousand falls below nothing, so the pledge is taken to nothing and the receipt is surrendered.

## Notes for the desk

**Is the sum ever allowed to fall below nothing?** It is not. The revised figure is taken to no less than nothing.

**Where does the rounding fall?** Once, on the total, and to two decimal places.
